# Decisions: commit-attribution

- 2026-08-13T08:01:32.455Z — rule: **Never record push, merge, or PR state as an event — derive it from git at read time. Only commit-to-initiative attribution is recorded.** — chose **Split the model: RECORD commit-to-initiative attribution in the log, DERIVE pushed/merged from git at read time. A commit's initiative never changes, so the recorded half can never go stale; push state changes constantly (force-push, rebase, branch deletion), so recording it would strand a false fact in an append-only log the moment anyone rewrites history.** over Recording push/merge/PR state as events alongside the attribution — the obvious symmetric design, and the one that silently rots. Also over deriving BOTH halves from git at read time, which cannot work: git has no idea which initiative a commit belongs to, and that is precisely the fact only sofar holds. because git is truth for git state; the log is truth for intent. Duplicating the first into the second is how a record starts lying. The whole point of this initiative is a staleness signal a session can trust — a signal built on recorded push state would itself be the next thing to go stale.
- 2026-08-13T08:01:40.172Z — chose **Attribute each commit individually, at commit time, when the session pin already names the initiative. Exact by construction.** over Deriving a phase's commits from session-boundary HEAD shas (record HEAD at session start; the range is startHEAD(N)..startHEAD(N+1)) and filtering that range by the initiative's file_touched set. Proposed and rejected inside the same design conversation on 2026-08-13. because The range design is a heuristic, and its two failure modes are fatal to gap 1. Concurrent sessions share this worktree, so any range contains peers' commits and the file-set filter is a guess that mis-attributes whenever two initiatives touch the same file — which the adjacency data says is the normal case here, not the edge case. And a claim like "this initiative's work is all pushed" cannot rest on a guess: a wrong "your work shipped" is worse than no signal, because it retires a next action that was never done. Separately, closing the range at session end is an off-by-one that would eat the most important commit of every session, since CLAUDE.md mandates write-back BEFORE the final commit.
- 2026-08-13T08:01:48.217Z — rule: **The review step names existing skills for code-quality checks and never reimplements them; sofar emits the prompt and records the verdict, never analyses code and never calls a model.** — chose **The review step is instruction text plus a record-derived evidence packet. sofar renders what to review, against which decisions, over which diff — and names the existing skills (/code-review, /simplify) for the code-quality half. The model reaches for those skills; sofar ships no analysis code and makes no model call.** over Building bug-hunting, edge-case and code-quality analysis into sofar itself — which would duplicate mature tools badly and drag a record-keeper into being a code analyzer, against CLAUDE.md's guard-rails. because Same pattern as the SessionStart digest: sofar injects text, the model acts. It keeps SPEC §Architectural invariants intact (zero model API calls) while still buying a real review. The one check with NO substitute is conformance to the record — whether the shipped code honoured the standing constraints and stayed out of the rejected approaches — because sofar is the only thing that holds them; /code-review cannot know a given decision exists.
